title.narrative: Support to the Professionalization of the Police for Population and Peace in the Democratic Republic of Congo (P4P, Phase 2)

description.narrative:
With regard to the participation of public or social institutions, the actions and activities planned as part of this collaboration will be carried out in conjunction with the Kimbanseke CLSP and with the participation of local, provincial and national institutions. Applying the principle of subsidiarity, UN-Habitat will delegate the design and delivery of the training modules to the most appropriate institutions. The training workshops will focus on civics and patriotic awareness for peace, andragogy and neighbourhood awareness, public order management, participatory budgeting and co-production of clean and safe places for the CLPS and FQ. Drafting of the Local Security Plan with the CLSP and the NGO RRSSJ, and of the interview guide with the help of the SGEI/ComGen for its appropriation. These activities will be carried out within the framework of a multi-stakeholder drafting committee to ensure that the various dimensions of the supply or demand for safety, or the maintenance of the quality or aesthetics of a building, are taken into account.
The non-exhaustive list of public institutions to be mobilised is as follows:
National institutions : - Ministries responsible for town planning and housing, land affairs, the environment and sustainable development, health and hygiene, youth and initiation into the new citizenship; - Congolese National Police (PNC) with the CRP (Cellule Réforme de la Police) as the entry point - Entrepreneurship Guarantee Fund (FOGEC), - University of Kinshasa (Faculty of Science and Technology, Department of Environmental Science and Management), - National Agency for the Development of Congolese Entrepreneurs (ANADEC) - National Agency for the Protection of State Property (AN-PPIE)
Provincial and local institutions : - Government of the city of Kinshasa - Provincial ministries responsible for education, the environment, health, security, civil protection, land and town planning. - Commissariat Provincial Kinshasa and Commissariat Urbain de la District du Tshangu - Kinshasa Urban Development Unit (CDUK) - RASKIN - the specialised services of the Commune of Kimbanseke - The neighbourhood chief's office, notables and street chiefs. - The NGO RRSSJ - recognised youth, women's, disabled and senior citizens' organisations.
From a financial point of view, and given the deadlines, UN-Habitat will promote the implementation of activities in a collegiate mode. The aim is to give those in charge of the CLSP, the neighbourhood, and the specialised services of the PNC (infrastructure and civil protection) the opportunity to take the co-lead in the design and execution of operations. The actions will be carried out with the technical support of UN-Habitat, which will also provide quality assurance through its advisers. The technical documents (terms of reference and working aids) for implementing the activities will be produced with the focal points of the said institutions.
A scoping meeting will be held before 30 December 2024 to brief the stakeholders and delegate the actions to be carried out in order to meet the deadlines. In January 2025, a second scoping meeting will be held to review and validate the tools. Two preparatory field visits will be carried out to identify and involve training institutions (schools, institutes) with the PNC, the CLSP, neighbourhood leaders and representatives of the relevant ministerial departments. Spatial analysis of the challenges of community safety, health, tranquillity and good morals will be mapped out to contribute to the development of the PLS.
Training or awareness-raising sessions will be offered at the end of January on approaches to developing a PLS, with the assistance of the RRSSJ, which helped set up the Kimbanseke CLSP. Experiences from other towns in the DRC will be presented by the PNC and other African towns will be presented by UN-Habitat experts. Between the end of January and mid-February 2025, the participatory drafting workshop for the Kimbaseke LSP will be held, again with the support of the RRSSJ and the PNC. The Local Safety Projects based on the finalised and validated LSP are scheduled to be implemented between mid-February and the end of March 2025. This approach will be used to produce the maintenance and management guide, a preliminary draft of which will be prepared by a consultant in consultation with the SGEI/ComGen. A preliminary draft will be prepared by a consultant in consultation and with the assistance of the SGEI/ComGen. It will be improved at a meeting based on observations of the current state of upkeep, maintenance and management of the PNC's buildings. This will take place in February. March 2025 will be devoted to proofreading and finalising the documents and producing the final reports. The indicative financial report will be available at the end of March, but the final report will be submitted three months after the end of the project.
